blocks.text: Setting up Google Sheets for shipping coordinators on Mac

There is no native Mac app for Google Sheets, but you can create one. Open Chrome and go to sheets.google.com. Click the three-dot menu in the top right corner. Select Cast, Save, and Share, then choose Install page as app. This creates a shortcut in your Applications folder. You can now launch your tracking sheets like any other native Mac program.
Essential keyboard shortcuts for logistics data

Shipping coordinators need speed. Press ⌘ + / to open the full list of shortcuts. Use ⌘ + ⇧ + H to find and replace outdated carrier info. If you need to hide rows with completed shipments, use ⌘ + ⌥ + 9. Use ⌘ + ⌥ + 0 to hide columns that contain sensitive pricing or internal notes.

items: Use ⌘ + ⇧ + H for quick find and replace across your entire shipment log.
Press ⌘ + ⌥ + 9 to hide rows containing delivered or archived cargo.
Use ⌘ + ⌥ + 0 to hide columns like internal cost rates when sharing with external partners.
Press Option + / to open the Tool Finder and search for any menu command.

blocks.text: Lazur helps you stay focused on your logistics tasks. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about a specific cell or function. If you need to know how to count unique carriers in a list, ask Lazur. It will explain the steps without you leaving the sheet.

Many coordinators run into trouble with broken formulas. If you see #N/A or #REF!, check your cell ranges. Ensure your carrier names are consistent to avoid errors in your tracking reports. Use data validation to create dropdown lists for carrier status updates. This prevents typos that break your formulas later.
How to handle large shipment datasets

Google Sheets now supports up to 20 million cells per file. However, performance can drop if you have too many complex formulas. If your sheet feels slow, convert static data to values. Copy your range, then use ⌘ + ⇧ + V to paste as values only. This removes the formula calculation burden while keeping your data.

faq.question: Is there a native Google Sheets app for macOS?
faq.answer: No, there is no official native app. You can create a web app shortcut using Google Chrome to get a similar experience.

faq.question: How do I speed up my workflow in Google Sheets?
faq.answer: Use keyboard shortcuts like ⌘ + / to find commands quickly and use the Tool Finder for specific tasks.
